statement: A continuous probability distribution for a real-valued random variable X with expected value (mean) μ and standard deviation σ (or variance σ²), denoted X ~ N(μ, σ²), defined by the probability density function f(x | μ, σ²) = (1 / σ) * φ((x - μ) / σ) = (1 / (σ * √(2π))) * e^(-(x - μ)² / (2σ²)), where φ(z) = (1 / √(2π)) * e^(-z² / 2) is the standard normal density.

symbols.meaning: real-valued argument / realization of the random variable
mean or expected value of the distribution
standard normal probability density function (mean 0, variance 1)
standard normal deviate, Z = (X - μ) / σ

properties.property: Standardization and affine transformation: X = σZ + μ where Z is a standard normal deviate with mean 0 and variance 1, and conversely Z = (X - μ) / σ.
properties.why: Scaling the standard normal variate by σ and shifting by μ yields a normal distribution with mean μ and standard deviation σ.

properties.property: Cumulative distribution function: F(x) = Φ((x - μ) / σ) = (1/2) * [1 + erf((x - μ) / (σ * √2))].
properties.why: The generic cumulative distribution function relates directly to the standard normal CDF Φ and the error function erf.

properties.property: Alternative precision parameterization: f(x) = √(τ / (2π)) * e^(-τ(x - μ)² / 2), where precision τ = 1 / σ².
properties.why: Precision defined as the reciprocal of the variance simplifies certain numerical and Bayesian computations.

properties.property: Symmetry of the standard normal CDF: Φ(-x) = 1 - Φ(x).
properties.why: The graph of Φ has 2-fold rotational symmetry around the point (0, 1/2).

properties.property: Empirical 68–95–99.7 rule: P(μ - nσ ≤ X ≤ μ + nσ) = Φ(n) - Φ(-n) = erf(n / √2), yielding ~68% for n=1, ~95% for n=2, and ~99.7% for n=3.
properties.why: Coverage probabilities for symmetric standard deviation intervals around the mean.

properties.property: Quantile function: F⁻¹(p) = μ + σ * Φ⁻¹(p) = μ + σ * √2 * erf⁻¹(2p - 1) for p ∈ (0, 1).
properties.why: Inverting the cumulative distribution function yields the quantiles in terms of the inverse error function.

assumptions.assumption: The scale parameter σ is strictly positive (σ > 0).
assumptions.breaks_when: σ ≤ 0, which makes 1/σ undefined or introduces division by zero in standardization.

assumptions.assumption: The random variable X is continuous and real-valued (X ∈ ℝ).
assumptions.breaks_when: The variable is discrete or restricted to complex or non-Euclidean spaces.

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero in normalization factor 1/σ and exponent (x - μ) / σ.
failure_modes.cause: σ = 0 or variance σ² = 0, collapsing the continuous density to a degenerate point mass.

failure_modes.mode: Taylor series divergence / slow convergence in practical calculation
failure_modes.signature: Ineffective or slow calculation when computing the CDF Φ(x) using its Taylor series expansion.
failure_modes.cause: Evaluating the Taylor series of Φ(x) at large values of x instead of small x.
